cells.tense: You are right here, letting a chapter finish that has already run its course.
cells.ask: Name one thing at home or at work that has run its course, and put a last date on it. The fairness is the act.
cells.core:
Something in your life is ending, and you are not pretending otherwise. You can feel the need for it, so you are letting it finish instead of keeping it breathing. What comes next is not forced, because you have not skipped the part where this one closes.

Fairness belongs in this. What you give and what you receive can sit side by side without fuss, and you adjust the scale without weighing every coin. The space gets cleared, and the clearing is what lets the next thing arrive.

Name one thing at home or at work that has run its course, and put a last date on it. The fairness is the act.
cells.sheetLine: You can let a thing finish and still keep it fair.
cells.verb: Ending what has run its course

cells.tense: You will have ended things next quarter that have not even been given their season.
cells.ask: Pick one ending you have already scheduled for later, and leave it alone until it actually asks to finish, without preparing the exit.
cells.core:
You are ending things ahead of schedule. Before this one has lived, you have already pictured the next chapter, and you are clearing rooms in the future. The liberation feels like relief, and it arrives too early, which makes it fear wearing its coat.

Real endings come out of what has been lived and felt, not out of what you are bracing for. When every chapter is cut short, nothing stays long enough to teach you what it was for, and you move on with the same unsettled thing.

Pick one ending you have already scheduled for later, and leave it alone until it actually asks to finish. Do not prepare the exit.
cells.sheetLine: You are ending things before they have had their life.

cells.tense: You were keeping a finished thing on the schedule, as if the door were still open.
cells.ask: Choose one finished thing you have kept active in your days, and make the smallest move that lets it be over, one gesture only.
cells.core:
Something ended and you stayed. You kept a version of it going because leaving felt like a break in the arrangement, and you can call that loyalty. There is another word on the tip of it, but it is yours to say, not mine.

Because the ending did not get written into your days, the new thing keeps waiting at the door. You have a foot back in a room that has already emptied, and the space it needs has not been made yet.

Choose one finished thing you have kept active in your days, and make the smallest move that lets it be over. One gesture, and finally done.
cells.sheetLine: You are keeping something alive that has already finished.

cells.tense: You have been writing the ending without knowing that your hand has been on the pen.
cells.ask: Name one thing in your life that has quietly changed shape this year, and say, once, that you are the one who changed it.
cells.core:
Something in you is already dying, and you have been describing it as someone else's decision. You talk about the ending as if it were handed to you, and you mark it in your calendar like a thing that happened to you. The writing has been going on while the pen stayed down.

You are not someone who needs convincing about structure. You make sense of rooms when the furniture is placed, and you can place it. The clearer version of this is simple: the ending is yours, and claiming it is the same as deciding what comes next.

cells.sheetLine: The ending is already yours. You just haven't claimed it.
